arxiv-2110-02294.title: Dynamic clustering of passive colloids in dense suspensions of motile bacteria
arxiv-2110-02294.creator: Shreyas Gokhale ‡,, Junang Li ‡,, Alexandre Solon, Jeff Gore, Nikta Fakhri
arxiv-2110-02294.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shreyas Gokhale ‡,, Junang Li ‡,, Alexandre Solon, Jeff Gore, Nikta Fakhri. Mixtures of active and passive particles are predicted to exhibit a variety of nonequilibrium phases. Here we report a dynamic clustering phase in mixtures of colloids and motile bacteria. We show that colloidal clustering results from a balance between bond breaking due to persistent active motion and bond stabilization due to torques that align active particle velocity tangentially to the passive particle surface.

arxiv-2201-04125.title: Spectrum Surveying: Active Radio Map Estimation with Autonomous UAVs Thanks: Research funded by the Research Council of Norway (IKTPLUSS grant 280835) and Department of Science and Technology, India. Emails: {raju.shrestha, daniel.romero}@uia.no, spchepuri@iisc.ac.in. Parts of this work were present
arxiv-2201-04125.creator: Raju Shrestha, Daniel Romero, Sundeep Prabhakar Chepuri
arxiv-2201-04125.description: Abstract Radio maps find numerous applications in wireless communications and mobile robotics tasks, including resource allocation, interference coordination, and mission planning. Although numerous techniques have been proposed to construct radio maps from spatially distributed measurements, the locations of such measurements are assumed predetermined beforehand.

arxiv-2205-10573.title: Spectral Neural Operators
arxiv-2205-10573.creator: Vladimir Fanaskov, Ivan Oseledets
arxiv-2205-10573.description: Abstract A plentitude of applications in scientific computing requires the approximation of mappings between Banach spaces. Recently introduced Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) and Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) can provide this functionality. For both of these neural operators, the input function is sampled on a given grid (uniform for FNO), and the output function is parametrized by a neural network.

arxiv-2206-14945.title: Continuously tracked, stable, large excursion trajectories of dipolar coupled nuclear spins
arxiv-2206-14945.creator: Ozgur Sahin, Hawraa Al Asadi, Paul M. Schindler, Arjun Pillai, Erica Sanchez, Matthew Markham, Mark Elo, Maxwell McAllister, Emanuel Druga, Christoph Fleckenstein, Marin Bukov, Ashok Ajoy
arxiv-2206-14945.description: Abstract We report an experimental approach to excite, stabilize, and continuously track Bloch sphere orbits of dipolar-coupled nuclear spins in a solid. We demonstrate these results on a model system of hyperpolarized C 13 {}^{13}\textrm{C} nuclear spins in diamond. Without quantum control, inter-spin coupling leads to rapid spin decay in T 2 ∗ ≈ 1.5 T_{2}^{\ast}{\approx}1.5 ms.

arxiv-2211-01969.title: Grounding Scene Graphs on Natural Images via Visio-Lingual Message Passing
arxiv-2211-01969.creator: Aditay Tripathi Anand Mishra Anirban Chakraborty
arxiv-2211-01969.description: Abstract This paper presents a framework for jointly grounding objects that follow certain semantic relationship constraints given in a scene graph. A typical natural scene contains several objects, often exhibiting visual relationships of varied complexities between them. These inter-object relationships provide strong contextual cues towards improving grounding performance compared to a traditional object query-only-based localization task.

arxiv-2401-11248.title: Drop your Decoder: Pre-training with Bag-of-Word Prediction for Dense Passage Retrieval. Conference: Proceedings of the 47th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 14–18, 2024; Washington, DC, USA Proceedings of the 47th International ACM SIGIR
arxiv-2401-11248.creator: Guangyuan Ma, Xing Wu, Zijia Lin, Songlin Hu
arxiv-2401-11248.description: Abstract . Masked auto-encoder pre-training has emerged as a prevalent technique for initializing and enhancing dense retrieval systems. It generally utilizes additional Transformer decoder blocks to provide sustainable supervision signals and compress contextual information into dense representations. However, the underlying reasons for the effectiveness of such a pre-training technique remain unclear.

arxiv-2410-17419.title: Design of the tertiary optical system for the LLAMA radio telescope
arxiv-2410-17419.creator: Emiliano Rasztocky, Matías Rolf Hampel, Rodrigo Reeves, Jacques R.D. Lepine, Gustavo Esteban Romero
arxiv-2410-17419.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Emiliano Rasztocky, Matías Rolf Hampel, Rodrigo Reeves, Jacques R.D. Lepine, Gustavo Esteban Romero. Many modern radio telescopes employ an observational strategy that involves maximizing the use of their available spaces (cabins), outfitting them with various receivers at different frequencies to detect incoming signals from the sky simultaneously or individually. The Large Latin American Millimeter Array (LLAMA), is a joint venture between Argentina and Brazil consisting of the installation and operation of a 12-meter aperture Cassegrain telescope.

arxiv-2501-12576.title: Mechanism Design for Blockchain Order Books against Selfish Miners
arxiv-2501-12576.creator: Yunshu Liu, Lingjie Duan, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2501-12576.description: Abstract In blockchain-based order book systems, buyers and sellers trade assets, while it is miners to match them and include their transactions in the blockchain. It is found that many miners behave selfishly and myopically, prioritizing transactions with high fees and ignoring many desirable matches that could enhance social welfare.

arxiv-2503-19207.title: FRESA: Feedforward Reconstruction of Personalized Skinned Avatars from Few Images
arxiv-2503-19207.creator: Rong Wang, Fabian Prada, Ziyan Wang, Zhongshi Jiang, Chengxiang Yin, Junxuan Li, Shunsuke Saito, Igor Santesteban, Javier Romero, Rohan Joshi, Hongdong Li, Jason Saragih, Yaser Sheikh, Australian National University
arxiv-2503-19207.description: Abstract We present a novel method for reconstructing personalized 3D human avatars with realistic animation from only a few images. Due to the large variations in body shapes, poses, and cloth types, existing methods mostly require hours of per-subject optimization during inference, which limits their practical applications.

arxiv-2505-11951.title: Reach-avoid games for players with damped double integrator dynamics footnoteinfo
arxiv-2505-11951.creator: Mengxin Lyu, Ruiliang Deng, Zongying Shi, Yisheng Zhong
arxiv-2505-11951.description: Abstract This paper investigates a reach–avoid game between two players with damped double integrator dynamics. An optimal state-feedback strategy is derived using a differential game framework combined with geometric analysis. To facilitate the analysis, we introduce the concept of multiple reachable region by characterizing the motion of players with damped double integrator dynamics.

arxiv-2507-19694.title: Ultracoarse Equilibria and Ordinal - Folding Dynamics in Operator - Algebraic Models of Infinite Multi - Agent Games
arxiv-2507-19694.creator: Faruk Alpay 1 Hamdi Alakkad 2 alpay@lightcap.ai hamdi.alakkad@bahcesehir.edu.tr Bugra Kilictas 2 Taylan Alpay 3 bugra.kilictas@bahcesehir.edu.tr s220112602@stu.thk.edu.tr 1 Independent Researcher 2 Bahcesehir University 3 Turkish Aeronautical Association University
arxiv-2507-19694.description: Abstract We develop an operator–algebraic framework for infinite games with a continuum of players and show how regret–minimising dynamics, driven by a noncommutative continuity equation, converge to a unique equilibrium under mild regularity conditions. Our work unifies functional analysis, coarse geometry, and game theory, extending earlier work on ultracoarse equilibria to incorporate ordinal metrics for self–referential dynamics.

arxiv-2512-06115.title: Formation of cold giant planets around late M dwarfs via core accretion and the fate of inner rocky worlds
arxiv-2512-06115.creator: M. Sanchez, N. van der Marel, M. Lambrechts, S. Paardekooper, Y. Miguel
arxiv-2512-06115.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. Sanchez, N. van der Marel, M. Lambrechts, S. Paardekooper, Y. Miguel. Modeling how cold giant planets form around M dwarfs remains a challenge, both because their protoplanetary disks can lack sufficient mass and because such planets are expected to migrate inward while interacting with the disk. Moreover, it remains unknown whether inner rocky planets can survive in systems that host a cold giant around very low-mass stars, which could have important implications for the habitability of rocky worlds.

pmc-11285441.creator: Patrick Kierkegaard, Bowen Su, Richard Wong, Marta Boffito, Suki Balendra
pmc-11285441.description: BackgroundThe set-up, activation, and delivery of clinical trials is pivotal for the advancement of medical science, serving as the primary mechanism through which new therapeutic interventions are validated for clinical use. Despite their critical role, the execution of these trials is often encumbered by a multitude of challenges.

pmc-11355887.title: The Co-Occurrence of 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome and Epithelial Basement Membrane Dystrophy: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
pmc-11355887.creator: Marta Armentano, Ludovico Alisi, Francesca Giovannetti, Valeria Iannucci, Luca Lucchino, Alice Bruscolini, Alessandro Lambiase
pmc-11355887.description: Background: 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11.2DS) is a genetic disorder caused by the deletion of the q11.2 band of chromosome 22. It may affect various systems, including the cardiovascular, immunological, gastrointestinal, endocrine, and neurocognitive systems. Additionally, several ocular manifestations have been described. Results: We report a case of a 34-year-old female diagnosed with 22q11.

pmc-11672829.title: Differential Biological Effects of Trifolium pratense Extracts—In Vitro Studies on Breast Cancer Models
pmc-11672829.creator: Lucian Albulescu, Alexandru Suciu, Mihaela Neagu, Cristiana Tanase, Sevinci Pop
pmc-11672829.description: The increasing popularity of herbal supplements emphasizes the need of scientific data regarding their health benefits and possible toxicological concerns. The complexity of botanical extracts, which include thousands of distinct compounds, contributes to the challenging nature of this endeavor. In this study, we explored the hormetic effects of two Trifolium pratense extracts on breast cell lines.

pmc-12446302.title: The relationship between fundamental motor skills and executive function in children: a stratified analysis by age and sex
pmc-12446302.creator: Chuifeng Kong, Yujun Cai, Kai Li, Zisu Wang, Xili Wen, Xinmiao Zhang
pmc-12446302.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to systematically examine the relationship between fundamental motor skills (FMS) and executive function (EF) in Chinese children aged 3 to 10 years. The study specifically focused on age and sex differences, as well as the associations between subcomponents of FMS and EF, to provide empirical evidence for research and intervention strategies targeting motor-cognitive integration in child development.

pmc-12542002.title: TCA-cycle metabolites in the nucleus: drivers of chromatin and epigenetic control
pmc-12542002.creator: Serena Ghisletti, Marta Russo
pmc-12542002.description: Mitochondrial enzymes are increasingly recognized for their ability to translocate to the nucleus, where they generate metabolites essential for epigenetic regulation and gene expression. Yet, whether this phenomenon broadly involves metabolic enzymes or is restricted to specific subunits remains unclear.

pmc-12729999.title: Protective Functions of β-Alanyl-L-Histidine and Glycyl-L-Histidyl-L-Lysine Glycoconjugates and Copper in Concert
pmc-12729999.creator: Irina Naletova, Enrico Rizzarelli, Ana-Maria Buga
pmc-12729999.description: Two endogenous peptides, β-alanyl-L-histidine, named carnosine (Car), and glycyl-L-histidyl-L-lysine (GHK), derived from the matricellular protein Secreted Protein Acidic and Rich in Cysteine (SPARC), share many beneficial functions. The hydrolytic enzyme carnosinase for Car and the low stability for GHK can put into question their antioxidant, antiaggregating, and anti-inflammatory properties.

pmc-12748309.title: Systematic literature reviews in migration studies: approaches to context-sensitive synthesis
pmc-12748309.creator: Tone Sommerfelt, Mathilde Bålsrud Mjelva, Jørgen Carling, Maryam Aslany
pmc-12748309.description: With a burgeoning literature on migration, taking stock of what is known about a topic, pattern, or process is challenging. In many scientific fields, systematic literature reviews (SLRs) are a widespread response to this need. In migration research, SLRs are relatively rare. Most existing literature reviews are non-systematic and often geographically specific.

pmc-13124278.title: Intra-articular allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cell injections for stage III knee osteoarthritis: a double-blind placebo-controlled trial with 60-month follow-up
pmc-13124278.creator: Hanan Jafar, Osama Samara, Diana Shahin, Fadwa Daoud, Dana Al-Hattab, Aseel Samara, Lina Al Lawama, Mohammed Hamdan, Huda Qubbaj, Bareqa Salah, Abdalla Awidi
pmc-13124278.description: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease with limited treatment options that effectively modify disease progression. This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of allogeneic adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (ADMSCs) injected under ultrasound guidance in patients with symptomatic stage III KOA.

pmc-13133595.title: Artificial Intelligence for Identifying Patient-Reported Outcome and Experience Measures in Oncology: Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study Using ClinicalTrials.gov
pmc-13133595.creator: Jessica Soyer, Akram Hecini, Sylvain Juchet, Céline Desvignes-Gleizes, Maxime Thiebaut, Jean-Philippe Bertocchio
pmc-13133595.description: BackgroundTraditional health care systems have evolved to increasingly recognize patients’ perspectives as key to improving the quality of care, especially in oncology. Hence, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and patient-reported experience measures (PREMs) can enhance patient–health care provider communication while facilitating individualized care.

pmc-13281216.title: Conflict and control in error monitoring during sustained visual discrimination
pmc-13281216.creator: Taylor M. Curley, L. Jack Rhodes, Lorraine Borghetti, Megan B. Morris
pmc-13281216.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Increases in response errors across time-on-task are ubiquitous in vigilance research, particularly for tasks that require visual operations. An important aspect of vigilance tasks is response monitoring, particularly when a prepotent response must be inhibited.

pmc-13444172.title: Dialysis modality and survival in octogenarians: real-world population-based cohort study
pmc-13444172.creator: Néstor Toapanta, María Antonieta Azancot, Jordi Comas, Natalia Ramos, Juan León-Román, Marc Patricio-Liébana, Jorge Sánchez Olaya, Tiffany Alvarez, Efraín Tatis, Sara Nuñez, Natalia Padron, Héctor Bedoya, Iván Zamora, Jaume Tort, Oriol Bestard, Francesc Moreso, María José Soler
pmc-13444172.description: BackgroundEvidence guiding dialysis modality decisions in very elderly patients is limited, and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized. This study evaluates long-term survival in octogenarians initiating kidney replacement therapy (KRT) by dialysis modality.MethodsWe used data from the Catalan Renal Registry to identify all patients aged ≥80 years who started dialysis between 2000 and 2022.

pmc-13634555.title: Post‐COVID‐19 Public Health Challenges: Insights Into Post‐COVID Symptoms, Stigma, and Post‐Pandemic Recovery Support From the Vietnam Experience
pmc-13634555.creator: Binh‐Minh Le Thi Nguyen, Truc Thanh Thai, Tri Nugraha Susilawati, Thanh Chi Vo, Mai Quynh Pham, Anh‐Thu Trang Thai, Nguyen Thao Dang, Nhan My Le, Thuy Anh Bui, Minh Cuong Duong
pmc-13634555.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to assess the burden of post‐COVID‐19 symptoms, social stigma, and quality of life, and to examine their interactions among individuals recovering from COVID‐19 in Vietnam.MethodsA cross‐sectional survey was conducted from March to June 2022 among individuals who had recovered from COVID‐19 within 1–3 months prior.
